strategy.title: Deliver the five signed phone-booth zone installs through QuietWall and keep $6,000 after supplier costs
strategy.why: Five operators signed fixed quotes at $2,600 per zone (EVIDENCE, Nov 20-27). QuietWall Installers LLC quoted $1,400 per zone in writing, materials included, two zones a week from Dec 1, and invoices net 3 after the client pays, so no capital is ever advanced (exposure $0). The five booked installs (Dec 1, 4, 8, 11, 15) fit QuietWall's two-a-week capacity; clients pay within 5 days of completion (last by day 22) and QuietWall is paid by day 25, inside the 30-day window. Net kept = 5 x ($2,600 - $1,400) = $6,000 >= $5,000. All five are needed (four would keep $4,800). Market volume is not a gap: the buyers are already signed, so Brain's parked buyerVolume question does not decide this plan.

reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is supported. Five coworking operators signed fixed quotes at $2,600 per zone (price fact EVIDENCE, five WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements), so no new deals are needed. Delivery is by the recorded fulfiller, QuietWall Installers LLC, on its written quote ($1,400 per zone incl. materials, two zones a week from Dec 1, invoices net 3 after the client pays), so nothing is paid before the client pays and exposure is $0 as the contract requires. Recomputed with today Nov 28 = day 0: installs Dec 1/4/8/11/15 = days 3/6/10/13/17 (two a week, inside QuietWall's capacity); client payments within 5 days settle days 8/11/15/18/22; QuietWall paid days 11/14/18/21/25, all inside 30. Contribution = 5 x ($2,600 - $1,400) = $6,000 >= $5,000; cash never goes negative because each supplier payment follows its client receipt. Ledger matches the steps and trace (collected $13,000, spent $7,000, net $6,000, max exposure $0). The parked buyerVolume question does not decide a plan whose buyers are already signed.
findings: Recomputed: 5 x $2,600 = $13,000 revenue, 5 x $1,400 = $7,000 supplier cost, $6,000 kept vs $5,000 target; proof day 25 of 30.
No deal slack: four zones keep $4,800 < $5,000, so one cancellation or one client paying more than ~8 days late on the last install misses the target. The plan states this; it is the residual risk.
Install dates sit exactly on QuietWall's two-per-week capacity; a slipped install pushes the last client payment toward the window end (last settles day 22, slack 8 days).
Owner hours ~1 per zone (card humanHours 1); no hours cap set.
Operational note: ISSUE_AN_INVOICE is NOT_CONNECTED; invoicing on completion must be connected before day 3.
